name: Wirrabara Producers Market
reason: Rule 4: a periodic producers market, not there whenever a visitor arrives.
objection: A genuine producers-only market a tourism board lists, but it runs on set days only.

name: Bundaleer Forest
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough); reservoir reserve 40 min from Clare. Counted source (flindersandoutback listing) opened: loop walk, kayak, fishing, picnic, open daily.
objection: Strong second-tier stop with two counted sources; if the proposer places Jamestown area under Flinders it should be kept.

name: Beetaloo Reservoir
reason: Rule 1-3: reservoir precinct near Port Pirie, two counted sources (flindersandoutback region page and listing, opened): open to the public for birdwatching, picnics, barbecues, fishing with permit.
objection: Ordinary water reserve; only half an hour of picnic and a look, and fishing permit needed.

name: Bendleby Ranges
reason: Rule 2: a working station stay with private 4WD and bike trails; the draw is accommodation, not a public place to visit.
objection: Source lists 180 km of trails and a regional blog names it, so day access could exist.

name: Horseshoe Top End
reason: Rule 1/2: a 4WD track named only in passing in a list of 4WD options; no visitor page describing it.
objection: May be a genuine 4WD route a local guide would recommend.

name: Jarvis Hill Lookout and Walking Trail
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) calls it a popular lookout 7 km west of Hawker with views to Wilpena Pound and the ranges. Against: one source, dirt road unsuitable when wet, short visit.
objection: Hawker already has Castle Rock and Camel Hump lookouts; near-duplicate stops.

name: Camel Hump Lookout Walk
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) describes an easy short climb 2 km south of Hawker with panoramic views, good for photographers. Against: one source, a short town-edge walk.
objection: Minor town-edge lookout, near-duplicate of Castle Rock and Jarvis Hill.

name: Castle Rock Walk and Lookout
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) names a prominent castle-shaped rock 2 km east of Hawker with a walking track and a late-light photo draw. Against: one source, short visit.
objection: Local landmark mostly for Hawker residents; one of three overlapping Hawker lookouts.

name: Devil's Peak Walking Trail
reason: Rule 2: the listing (opened) says it is on private property, 1.3 km each way, and gives no location or access, so cannot be treated as open to the public.
objection: It is a promoted walking trail with a 2-hour return time.

name: Ferguson Gorge Scenic Drive and Bush Walk
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) describes a scenic drive through Hannigans Gap and a 1.6 km walk to a gorge with rock pools and yellow-footed rock-wallabies, open to day visitors (4-5 hours). Against: private Moolooloo Station, pay at the homestead, one source.
objection: Operator-run on a station with accommodation; access is by payment to a business.

name: Magnetic Hill
reason: Rule 3 quirky roadside icon: counted listing (opened) calls it a quirky, well-known attraction near Orroroo where vehicles seem to roll uphill, a highlight of a 44 km self-drive loop.
objection: A ten-minute optical illusion on a dirt road, one source.

name: Louden Brae School
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). Also a small restored schoolhouse (listing opened) with only the R.M. Williams link.
objection: Counted tourism listing names it as a historic site.

name: Old Timers Mine
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-outback (Old Timers Mine is in Coober Pedy). Also an operator.
objection: A genuine Coober Pedy attraction; should be kept under the outback region.

name: Red Bridge
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) presents the 1882 Red Bridge over Pekina Creek as a surviving railway landmark in Orroroo. Against: one source, a short look at a bridge.
objection: A minor heritage bridge on a town creek that most visitors would pass.

name: Early Settlers Cottage (Solly's Hut)
reason: Rule 2: open by appointment only (listing opened), a small local museum cottage; not there whenever one arrives.
objection: Counted listing names it, and a visit can run as long as one likes.

name: Diggers Walk Belalie Creek
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). A creek heritage trail with WWI interpretive displays (listing opened).
objection: Interesting walk with Hubert Wilkins story; one counted source.

name: Living in the Rangelands Trail
reason: Rule 2: a privately marked trail for guests of Skytrek Willow Springs Station only (listing opened).
objection: 12 km trail with a tourism listing.

name: Reedy Creek Trail
reason: Rule 2: a privately marked trail for Skytrek Willow Springs Station guests only (listing opened).
objection: 7.4 km trail with a tourism listing.

name: Orroroo Magpie Trail
reason: Rule 3: a geocaching trail through Orroroo town; not a distinct place, town-level activity with only passing counted mentions.
objection: Two counted sources mention it.

name: Jamestown Mural Walk and Outdoor Gallery
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). A town mural walk with a festival outdoor gallery (listing opened).
objection: Two-part mural walk a guide lists.

name: Jamestown Railway Station Museum
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). A railway station museum in Jamestown (listing opened).
objection: Counted listing describes interesting displays.

name: R.M. Williams Story (Jamestown)
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Jamestown/Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). An outdoor interpretive display in Robinson Park, Jamestown (listing opened).
objection: R.M. Williams is an Australian icon.

name: Fred Teague's Museum
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) describes a compact open museum at Hawker Motors with gemstones, minerals and fossils from the ranges and Waukaringa. Against: one source, a private collection in a service station.
objection: A small private collection inside a motors garage, mostly a stop for Hawker passers-by.

name: R J Finlayson Butter Factory
reason: Rule 2/3: listing (opened) says the building is empty and only a stop on the Gladstone Heritage Walk.
objection: A tourism listing exists for it.

name: Walloway Train Memorial
reason: Rule 3: a minor memorial plaque site to a 1901 train collision (listing opened).
objection: Counted listing frames it as a place of reflection 10 km from Orroroo.

name: Aboriginal Carvings
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) names Pekina Creek Aboriginal rock carvings as a short walk from Orroroo main street, a significant cultural heritage site. Against: one source, a short visit, few details of access.
objection: Engraving sites need cultural sensitivity and may be hard for visitors to find without a guide.

name: Hawker Heritage Walk
reason: Rule 3: a town self-guided heritage walk that is part of Hawker itself (duplicate of the town); the listing (opened) only points to a guide brochure.
objection: Two counted sources name it.

name: Adnyamathanha Dreaming Hawker Mural Walking Trail
reason: Case for: counted listing (opened) is a self-guided mural walk of Adnyamathanha Dreaming stories by Juanella McKenzie with dual-language labels. Against: one source, a town street-art trail.
objection: Overlaps a town stop and is a street walk rather than a place.

name: Jeff Morgan Gallery (Hawker)
reason: Rule 2: a private gallery/shop named only in an itinerary blog.
objection: Murals mentioned.

name: Flinders Food Co (Hawker)
reason: Rule 2: a cafe, named only in an itinerary blog.
objection: Local food stop in a remote town.

name: Cradock Heritage Walk
reason: Rule 1/3: Cradock Heritage Walk named only in a blog list; a walk through a tiny settlement, no visitor page.
objection: Cradock is a historic ghost-town stop on the Outback route.

name: Aroona Dam
reason: Rule 1-3: counted Leigh Creek town page (opened) describes Aroona Dam Sanctuary with fishing, views, picnic and a 5.5 km interpretive walk; the regional blog also names it for kayaking (open to non-motorised craft).
objection: A modest dam; one town-page paragraph and a blog.

name: Ajax Mine Fossil Reef
reason: Rule 2: a heritage-listed fossil site on the Puttapa pastoral lease; searches found no public access or visitor page, access only on guided tours.
objection: Internationally significant Cambrian fossil site that is part of the Flinders Ranges World Heritage bid.

name: Buckaringa Sanctuary
reason: Rule 1: no counted visitor source found after searching (AWC sanctuary page returned 404; only Wikipedia and non-counted ExplorOz). UNRESOLVED if AWC page exists.
objection: AWC sanctuary with a public scenic drive and lookout and a yellow-footed rock-wallaby colony; may deserve review if a counted source turns up.

name: Bunkers Conservation Reserve
reason: Rule 3: private conservation reserve whose visitor draw is the Caernarvon Track, listed separately; duplicate of that track.
objection: The reserve manager takes visitors for camping.

name: Horrocks Pass
reason: Case for: the counted Wilmington town page (opened) points to Horrocks Pass Road and Hancocks Lookout with views to Spencer Gulf; the pass has a Horrocks monument and lookout. Against: one passing mention, the lookout is the real stop.
objection: Scenic road and a monument; Hancocks Lookout may be the actual spot and the pass a drive.

name: Kanalla Falls
reason: Rule 1: no counted source; a waterfall inside Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park (part of a larger spot), seasonal flow.
objection: Wikipedia article exists and it is a named feature.

name: Mount Serle
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; a peak on a pastoral station.
objection: Historic Eyre landmark.

name: Mount Hack
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; the summit sits in the private Warraweena conservation reserve.
objection: Highest point of the reserve.

name: Mount Gee
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; a remote peak in the Arkaroola area.
objection: Wikipedia-only.

name: Baroota Dam
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; a water reservoir with no visitor page.
objection: Reservoir beside Mount Remarkable National Park.

name: Warratyi
reason: Rule 2: an archaeological rock shelter with no public access and no visitor source.
objection: Globally significant site.

name: Moolawatana Station
reason: Rule 2: a pastoral station; no counted source and no public visit.
objection: Historic station.

name: Wooltana Station
reason: Rule 2: a pastoral station; no counted source and no public visit.
objection: Historic station.

name: Willochra Creek
reason: Rule 1/3: a creek; no counted source.
objection: Wikipedia-only.

name: Rawnsley Park Heli-Camping
reason: Operators rule: a heli-camping experience from a station, a business rather than a place.
objection: Named in the regional nature blog.

name: Flinders Ranges Self-Drive Loop
reason: Rule 3: a touring route/brochure (listing opened) rather than a place; the stops are separate candidates.
objection: Counted source names it.

name: The Outback Loop
reason: Rule 3: a multi-track touring region (Birdsville, Strzelecki, Oodnadatta tracks; listing opened) rather than a place; belongs mostly to sa-outback.
objection: Two counted sources name it.

name: Quorn Historic Building Walk
reason: Rule 3: a self-guided brochure walk that is part of Quorn town (duplicate of the town); listing opened.
objection: Counted listing names it.

name: Powell Gardens
reason: Rule 3: a small native garden in Quorn parklands (listing opened); a local park. Wikipedia coordinates refer to a Missouri garden of the same name, so the match is wrong.
objection: Counted listing names it.

name: Terowie
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-barossa-clare (Mid North wheatbelt south of Peterborough). Historic railway town; the heritage walk and museums (web search) make it a good keep there. Counted source not confirmed.
objection: A historic town with a heritage walk and museums, worth keeping under the Mid North.
